answer_text:
To compute

\[
\operatorname{tr}(\exp(A)),
\]

we use the fact that if \(A\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\), then \(\exp(A)\) has eigenvalues \(e^{\lambda_1}, e^{\lambda_2}, e^{\lambda_3}\), so

\[
\operatorname{tr}(\exp(A)) = e^{\lambda_1}+e^{\lambda_2}+e^{\lambda_3}.
\]

Now compute the eigenvalues of

\[
A=\begin{bmatrix}
0 & -1 & 1\\
-1 & 0 & 1\\
1 & 1 & 0
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

The characteristic polynomial is

\[
\det(A-\lambda I)=
\begin{vmatrix}
-\lambda & -1 & 1\\
-1 & -\lambda & 1\\
1 & 1 & -\lambda
\end{vmatrix}.
\]

Expanding,

\[
\det(A-\lambda I)
= -\lambda(\lambda^2-1)+(\lambda-1)+(\lambda-1)
= -\lambda^3+3\lambda-2.
\]

Thus

\[
\det(A-\lambda I)
= -(\lambda^3-3\lambda+2)
= -(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda+2).
\]

So the eigenvalues are

\[
\lambda_1=1,\qquad \lambda_2=1,\qquad \lambda_3=-2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\operatorname{tr}(\exp(A))
= e^1+e^1+e^{-2}
= 2e+e^{-2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2e+e^{-2}}
\]
